A facet_grid() that can free scales panel by panel

Source: R/facet-gridn.R
facet_gridn.Rd

facet_gridn() lays panels out exactly like ggplot2::facet_grid() (rows and columns of facets, row strips on the right, column strips on top), but scales = "free_x" / "free_y" / "free" free the axis for every single panel instead of once per column / row. Each panel then trains its own scale on its own data, gets its own axis range and its own axis labels.

Usage

facet_gridn(
  rows = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  scales = "fixed",
  space = "fixed",
  shrink = TRUE,
  labeller = "label_value",
  as.table = TRUE,
  switch = NULL,
  drop = TRUE,
  margins = FALSE,
  axes = "margins",
  axis.labels = "all"
)

FacetGridN

Format

An object of class FacetGridN (inherits from FacetGrid, Facet, ggproto, gg) of length 3.

Arguments

rows, cols

A set of variables or expressions quoted by ggplot2::vars() and defining faceting groups on the rows or columns dimension.

scales

One of "fixed" (default), "free_x", "free_y" or "free" for per-panel freedom, or "free_x_bycol" / "free_y_byrow" for the stock facet_grid() behaviour (x per column, y per row).

space

If "fixed", all panels have the same size. If "free_x", "free_y" or "free", panel size is proportional to the panel's own range on that axis (this pairs naturally with per-panel scales).

shrink

If TRUE, will shrink scales to fit output of statistics, not raw data. Passed on to ggplot2::facet_grid().

labeller

A function that takes one data frame of labels and returns a list or data frame of character vectors.

as.table

If TRUE (the default), facets are laid out like a table, with the highest value in the bottom-right corner.

switch

By default, the labels are displayed on the top and right of the plot. Set to "x", "y" or "both" to move them.

drop

If TRUE (the default), unused factor levels are dropped.

margins

Passed on to ggplot2::facet_grid().

axes, axis.labels

Where to draw axes and labels, as in ggplot2::facet_grid(). The defaults ("margins") are what facet_grid() uses; when an axis is freed per panel the matching axes are drawn for every panel regardless, because one axis per row / column could not label the other cells.

Value

A FacetGridN ggproto object, usable in the same places as ggplot2::facet_grid().

Details

The two stock behaviours are still available as "free_x_bycol" and "free_y_byrow": they free x per column / y per row exactly like facet_grid(), which is handy when one figure has to mix both kinds of freedom.

How it differs from facet_grid()

facet_grid(scales = "free_x") frees x per column: panels stacked in the same column still share one x scale, because the layout assigns SCALE_X = COL. facet_gridn() assigns SCALE_X = PANEL, so every cell of the grid is independent:

scalesfacet_gridn()x scaley scale
"fixed"shared (default)one globalone global
"free_x"per panelone per panelone global
"free_y"per panelone globalone per panel
"free"per panelone per panelone per panel
"free_x_bycol"same as facet_grid()one per columnone global
"free_y_byrow"same as facet_grid()one globalone per row

Because a panel's range is its own, panels are no longer comparable through a shared axis: read each panel's own axis labels. "fixed" is unchanged, so a figure can switch between the two without touching anything else.

See also

ggplot2::facet_grid(), ggplot2::facet_wrap()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)

# Continuous: each panel gets its own x AND y range
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_gridn(vars(cyl), vars(gear), scales = "free")

# Same data with the stock facet: x is shared per column
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(vars(cyl), vars(gear), scales = "free_x")

# Categorical axes: each panel keeps only its own categories
ggplot(mpg, aes(class, hwy)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_gridn(vars(drv), vars(year), scales = "free_x")
} # }
